manifest.name: dsh-recent-tasks
manifest.description: A collapsible Recent tasks block at the section level of the DSH sidebar: chats with no workspace land there instead of piling up in 未分组 / DSH 侧边栏里与「工作区」同级、可独立折叠的「最近任务」区块：没有工作区的对话自动归到这里。

bundle.text:
# dsh-recent-tasks bundle patch: ONE row for a dual-face package.
#
# The row `name` is this package itself, so the host Loader imports its host half
# (`exports["."]`) AND the web-modules scanner discovers its browser half through
# the `dsh.client` declaration + `exports["./client"]` of the same package.json.
# One row, both halves -- the shape used by dsh-image-gen / dsh-paste-spill.
#
# `config` here reaches ONLY the host half; a bundle client half is created with
# `{ name: id }` and never receives row config, so the client half reads every
# tunable over `/dsh-recent-tasks/api/*` instead.
#
# THE ROW ID IS ALSO THE SETTINGS NAMESPACE. `recentTasksDir`, `title` and
# `autoRepair` are declared `.volatile()` in the host Config, so the official
# settings surface derives a form for this row automatically and writes edits
# into the ACTIVE PROFILE's cordis.patch.yml (never into this file, and never
# through a private config file). Those edits hot-apply: the loader commits them
# into the running Volatile refs and emits `loader/volatile-update`, which the
# host half listens to. `enabled` and `apiPrefix` are NOT volatile -- changing
# either remounts the row.
#
# Every key below is optional; the values are the documented defaults.
- insert:
    - id: recent-tasks
      name: dsh-recent-tasks
      config:
        # Where chats with no workspace are grouped. `~` is expanded against the
        # DSH host user's home. Change it in Settings -> General ("最近任务") or in
        # Settings -> Plugins; the new value lands in the profile patch layer.
        recentTasksDir: "~/Documents/DSH 最近任务"
        # Group name used when the workspace record is created. While the STORED
        # title is still one of this plugin's own default names (最近任务 / Recent
        # tasks) the client half keeps it in step with the UI language, because
        # the sidebar row and the workspace switcher render the durable title
        # verbatim. A sidebar rename -- or any other value here -- is treated as
        # user intent and is never rewritten.
        title: "最近任务"
        # Recreate the workspace record if it was deleted from the sidebar.
        autoRepair: true
        # Master switch. Patch-only: no settings form is generated for it.
        enabled: true
        # Host API path; patch-only, and must be a single absolute segment.
        apiPrefix: "/dsh-recent-tasks/api"

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[](LICENSE)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-recent-tasks)
[](package.json)
[](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

A collapsible **「最近任务」/ Recent tasks** block at the section level of the DeepSeek Harness sidebar. Chats that have no workspace land there instead of piling up in **未分组** — and because the block is a *real* workspace record rather than a look-alike drawn by a plugin, a chat started from it genuinely belongs to it.

DSH groups every chat under the workspace its session `cwd` resolves to. A chat started without a workspace gets no group at all, so it falls into the `未分组` bucket together with archived folders and deleted projects. This plugin registers **one real workspace record** for a dedicated folder: "no workspace" becomes an ordinary group with ordinary behaviour — rename, drag order, pin, archive, search — and that group is *promoted* into a collapsible block of its own, level with **工作区** and collapsing independently of it.

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| Group | A genuine `workspace` record for `<recentTasksDir>`, registered through `ctx.workspaceRegistry` and created as the last group; the plugin never rewrites the durable order afterwards, so where you drag it is where it stays |
| Entry | `＋ 最近任务对话` beside Settings at the sidebar foot, plus the `Mod+Alt+N` / `Mod+Shift+N` shortcut — both start a session in that workspace |
| Settings | The `最近任务` tab of **Settings → 内置插件** — folder, group name, auto-repair — backed by this plugin's official live config |
| Host API | `POST /dsh-recent-tasks/api/state` and `/ensure`, read-only and idempotent; the only write path is the official settings form |

The block behaves like any other group: `GPT-6 特点介绍` is the chat that is running right now, older ones show how long ago they were used, and `＋ 最近任务对话` at the sidebar foot starts a new chat in that folder. (This capture predates the promotion to a section-level block; the section below describes how the list reads now.)

The alternative — a plugin-drawn group — cannot work: the sidebar's groups *are* the `workspace` storage domain, and no slot lets a third-party plugin insert a parallel group. Registering a record instead of shadowing the sidebar means:

readme.section: Sidebar hierarchy: Recent tasks is its own block
readme.text: `最近任务` reads as a block-level section beside the official workspaces heading, and the two collapse independently: the arrow in front of "Workspaces" hides the *other* workspace groups (Recent tasks stays), while the arrow in front of "Recent tasks" collapses its own chats, which sit one indent step in from its title.

readme.text:
- This is presentation only: the group is still one real workspace record, and the plugin writes no workspace data — it neither reorders the list nor touches any group but its own.
- It keys on official *stable* attributes (`data-row-key`, `role`, the inline `--dsh-workspace-indent`) and never on official class names, which are build hashes that change between releases. If a DSH update moves those anchors the promotion **disables itself**: the sidebar falls back to the stock look with nothing left behind, one line in the console.
- It also stands down for the flat list, while searching, in the 56px rail, and in tree mode when the folder is nested under another workspace (then it is not a peer). Switching back re-applies it immediately.
- Known trade-offs: the block scrolls with the workspace list; while "Workspaces" is collapsed the highlight of a chat inside a hidden group is not visible until you expand it again; and on the single frame in which the official UI re-renders the container (before our replay runs) a collapsed group can flash back into view.
- The collapse flag lives in your own browser storage (`dsh.recent-tasks.workspaces-collapsed.v1`); it is never reported anywher

- [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) with a `web` or `desktop` profile, `0.2.0-rc.1` or newer (developed and verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`, cordis `~4.0.4`)
- Node.js `>= 22.19.0` — only to build from source
- [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) is recommended when installing into a profile
- No network access, no native modules, no install scripts, no runtime dependencies
> The bundle entry (`id: recent-tasks`) is self-declared by this package's `cordis.patch.yml` — no manual patch file is needed.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-recent-tasks
```

Published on npm as [`dsh-recent-tasks`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-recent-tasks). The package declares its `repository`, so the plugin market matches it back to this repo and can offer version and download information; installs are prebuilt and skip the build-approval step entirely. This is the path the plugin market prefers.

Install by **repository identity** to get the tip of `main` — useful for trying an unreleased change, and it is also how the plugin market resolves this package to `winditer/dsh-recent-tasks` when npm is not used:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:winditer/dsh-recent-tasks
```

For a web profile use `--profile web`. Restart DSH (quit fully and reopen); the 最近任务 group appears at the foot of the sidebar.

The built browser half (`dist/client.js`) is **committed** on purpose. A `github:` install never runs this package's build — pnpm blocks lifecycle scripts by default — so the committed bundle is what makes this install path work out of the box. Nothing is compiled on the consuming side.

**Settings → Plugins → install bundle**, pointing at this directory (or a `file:` spec). The script `scripts/install-into-profile.sh` is the manual equivalent: `pnpm add file:<repo>` plus a `dsh.profile.bundles` entry.

**The `dependencies` entry is not optional** — a bundle listed only in `dsh.profile.bundles` is erased by the desktop crash-recovery path, which re-derives the list from `dependencies`.

Every release attaches the packed package, so the whole repository is not downloaded and nothing is compiled on the consuming side:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/winditer/dsh-recent-tasks/releases/download/v0.4.1/dsh-recent-tasks-0.4.1.tgz
```

The URL is pinned to the tag rather than written as `releases/latest/download/…` on purpose: `latest` resolves per request but the filename is literal, so a versioned asset name breaks that URL the moment the next release renames it.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/winditer/dsh-recent-tasks.git && cd dsh-recent-tasks
npm install
npm run build          # regenerates dist/client.js
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .

`dist/client.js` is regenerated by `node scripts/build.mjs` before every launch; if it is ever missing, the host half still loads and the app logs `client bundle not found; run \`pnpm run build\` before launch`.

All three live rows are ordinary official settings, and they live in exactly one place: the **最近任务** tab of **Settings → 内置插件**, beside 插件列表 and 插件市场. The values are this plugin's own live `Config`; the tab writes through `configForms`, the same document the profile keeps.

Upgrading from 0.3.x: those settings used to sit in **Settings → 通用设置**. That row is gone — the keys, the defaults and the file the values live in are unchanged.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `recentTasksDir` | `~/Documents/DSH 最近任务` | Folder the group owns. Created on first use; must stay an absolute path. Changing it registers/uses the record for the new folder immediately. |
| `title` | `最近任务` | Group name used when a record is created. While the stored title is still one of this plugin's own default names (`最近任务` / `Recent tasks`) it follows the UI language; any other title is yours and is never rewritten. |
| `autoRepair` | `true` | Recreate the record if it was deleted from the sidebar. Switching it off turns deletion into a visible error instead of a silent rebuild. |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch (patch only — no form). |
| `apiPrefix` | `/dsh-recent-tasks/api` | Host API path (patch only). |

Edits are persisted by `dsh-config-editor` into the **active profile's** `cordis.patch.yml` (atomic write, validation, rollback) and hot-apply to the running host: the loader commits new values into the plugin's live `Volatile` refs and emits `loader/volatile-update`, which the host half uses to re-ensure immediately. This plugin never writes a config file of its own.

Precedence: the profile patch layer wins over this package's bundled defaults, so a user edit survives upgrades.

- **The API is small and local.** Two idempotent POSTs (`state`, `ensure`) requiring `content-type: application/json`; the JSON-only rule is also the CSRF defence, since a cross-site "simple request" cannot set that type without a preflight this route never answers. Nothing secret is exposed and the plugin never accepts a path or a command from the browser.
- **Failure is never silent.** Every refusal is a code (`bad-config`, `dir-not-writable`, `dir-not-directory`, `missing-record`, `disabled`, `unavailable`, …) which the client renders from this plugin's own locale namespace; the host never ships display text.
- **State is read-only.** `state` never mkdirs, never creates, never reorders — a vanished record is reported (`workspaceId: null` + `missing-record`) and only `ensure` repairs it.
- **Reuse over creation.** If the configured folder is already a workspace, that record is reused and its title is left alone (DSH's `create` is idempotent per `realpath` and ignores the title for an existing record).
- **Placed last, once.** DSH's `create` *prepends* a new record, so a freshly installed plugin would otherwise drop its block above every workspace you already own. The plugin there

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| No 最近任务 group appears | Check **Settings → 内置插件 → 最近任务** for a coded reason; `missing-record` + auto-repair off, or `dir-not-writable`. |
| The group is nested under another workspace | `recentTasksDir` is inside a registered workspace — pick a folder outside every workspace. |
| The entry point says `unavailable` | The host half is not mounted (row disabled, or the row mounted before `workspaceRegistry`). Reload the app once after installing. |
| Settings row shows the read-only hint | No `configForms` in this composition (no official settings surface); edit the `recent-tasks` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. |
| Chats still land in 未分组 | They were created *without* this workspace's `cwd`. Existing chat history is never migrated (design §6.3/N3): the group owns new chats started through the entry or the shortcut. |
| The block sits *above* the workspaces I already had | An install that predates the placement fix (0.3.0 relied on `create`, which prepends). The plugin only appends a record **it just created** — re-appending an existing one would undo your own drag — so drag the block below them once. |

```bash
node scripts/build.mjs      # build dist/client.js
node --test test/*.test.js  # 75 tests: protocol, host, client logic, sidebar section adapter, bundle contract
node scripts/build.mjs && node --test test/*.test.js   # = npm run verify
npm pack --dry-run          # inspect the published file list

`node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*` are symlinks into the extracted `0.2.0-rc.1` tree under `.asar/`, which only exists so `node --test` can resolve `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`; production resolves those specifiers through DSH's own profile interception, so the package declares them as *optional* peers and ships no runtime dependency.

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/host.js` → `lib/index.js` | Host half: `Config`, the registry service, the JSON API, the volatile-config listener |
| `src/client.js` → `dist/client.js` | Browser half: sidebar entry, settings row, refresh loop, shortcut |
| `src/client-core.js` | React-free logic: state machine, `planCreate`, snapshot store, shortcut resolution, collapse flag, promotion predicate |
| `src/client-adapter.js` | Sidebar section adapter: locates the official nodes at runtime, stamps `data-dsh-rt-*`, injects the collapse toggle, replays on re-render (presentation only, writes no data) |
| `src/protocol.js` | Shared vocabulary: codes, methods, path handling, response parsing |
| `src/locales.js` | `recentTasks` zh/en dictionaries (flat keys, 1:1 key sets) |
| `assets/` | Screenshots used by this README (and picked up by the plugin market) |
| `screenshots.json` | The screenshot list the plugin market reads (its convention: declared beside `package.json`, paths relative to the repo) |
| `test/` | `protocol` · `host` · `client` · `adapter` (hand-rolled DOM) · `bundle` |
| `docs/superpowers/` | This repo's own specs and implementation plans (`specs/`, `plans/`) |
